title: Live Preview trust proof set
note: Declarative manifest consumed by tools/lp-trust-runner.js. It asserts ABOUT the existing
tests; it never replaces them. No test or engine file is touched by this harness.
The gate is not 'the tests are green' — it is 'the proof still EXISTS'. Deleting a proof's
tests makes the plain suite greener; here it fails as proof-unbacked (see minCount).
Counts below were measured on this tree (origin/main @71340b2, extension 0.16.78), never cited.

classifyFreeze.why: S0 mirrors .github/workflows/test.yml — the frozen classifier is a repo-wide invariant.

why: The receipt is a PROJECTION of a run, never a source of truth. A committed receipt is a
stale claim that outlives the run that earned it, so the runner fail-closes if the path is
not git-ignored. Same pattern as _handoff/agent-sync/ and _handoff/loop/* in .gitignore.

skipAllowlist.namePattern: ^prepared content lease hashes a real symlink target
skipAllowlist.reason: Symlink creation needs elevation on Windows; the test runs for real on the CI ubuntu runner. Documented in the spec as the only known skip. NOTE: this file is not in the proof set, so this entry is currently inert — it is kept so the policy stays declarative if the file is ever pulled in.

proofs.name: Origin lease — an origin swap voids root+selection and bumps the epoch

match.note: Origin swap voids root+selection; same-origin HMR survives (negative control); a pending prompt-apply across the swap writes nothing; the new origin stays blocked until a fresh lp-ready.
Server up but identity unproven → readiness.tree === 'unknown', never absent.
Adversarial epoch race: a write echoing an OLD epoch refuses even on a reconfirmed tree. 4 present today; floor is the 1 the spec names.

proofs.name: SHA-guard on undo/revert and stale apply
proofs.backing: No open finding — this is a CERTIFIED INVARIANT (spec :360), i.e. a regression lock, not a fix. Said plainly.
residualRisk: P2 has NO formal finding ID embedded in its test names, so it is matched by BEHAVIOUR regex
instead of an ID prefix. A determined rename can still escape it. This weakness is declared
here, in the manifest, rather than hidden in a habit. Spec follow-up F7 (give the SHA-guard a
formal ID, e.g. INV-01, and put it in the test names) closes this — F7 edits test files, so it
is explicitly OUT of this wave's allowlist and stays open.

match.note: applyUndo is sha-gated; a foreign write after ours → undo-stale, nothing written, entry kept; a changed served tree → preview-tree-mismatch.

Stale TEXT/CLASS apply fail-closes writing nothing; apply without the preview hash is bad-request. The spec's published regex (sha-guarded|undo-stale|preview-tree-mismatch|bad-request) matched only 1 of the 3 tests in this file — the two FAIL-CLOSED titles carry no such token — so it would have failed its own minCount:5. Corrected here against the real titles.

proofs.name: Security fail-closed — no scan / failed / stale / Critical never spawns

match.note: Each asserts r.reason AND that vercel is never spawned: critical-open · overrideCritical IGNORED · security-scan-required · security-scan-failed · security-scan-stale · npm-audit prod critical. 11 D6 tests present today; floor is the 6 the spec names.

proofs.name: Publish only with explicit acceptance — a forged payload authorizes nothing
residualRisk: MEASURED DEVIATION FROM THE SPEC: spec §5 claims P2 is the only proof without a finding ID.
It is not. P4's tests carry NO ID prefix either ('Publish approval gate is global…',
'A forged Publish payload…') — no COH-10:, no D6 . So the manifest anchors 5/7 proofs by ID,
not 6/7 as the spec states. P4 therefore uses the same behaviour-regex fallback as P2, and
carries the same rename risk. Declared, not hidden. F7 should cover P4 as well as P2.

match.note: The approval gate is global: node A pending still vetoes while node B is selected.
A forged payload authorizes neither parallel files outside approval nor pre-existing dirt in the exact same approved path.
Vercel deploy requires the status identity lease even when the visible project name matches.
Production deploy refuses the mutable workspace until this panel has pushed an immutable commit.

proofs.name: Zero writes outside the preview path
proofs.backing: COH-01 §6:164 ('can edit the workspace while the iframe shows another app') · D2 :74

match.note: A sibling/null servedRoot refuses in _applyEdit/_deleteNode/_promptApply/_taskRun; _promptEdit refuses BEFORE shipping node bytes to the model. 9 present today; floor is the 8 the spec names.
The twin-worktree incident regression asserts the workspace target is left BYTE-IDENTICAL. Carries no G2: prefix, so it is matched by behaviour.

proofs.name: Telemetry honesty — a cloud/agent event is never local:true
proofs.backing: COH-08 (P1) :58 — 'the cost/model narrative becomes materially false'

match.note: An agent/cloud event carries the real tier/model and is never local:true; local:false is inferred from a cloud tier; a deploy event is never local.
The lifecycle phase rides the event (started/succeeded/failed/cancelled).

proofs.name: Lease revalidation on Ask→Apply
proofs.why: The only write path whose id comes from the webview. Without it P1's lease has a bypass and a green P1 would OVERSTATE the safety.

match.note: An unknown/expired askId refuses; a valid apply composes from the STORED question+answer and ignores a tampered payload; apply is one-shot. 7 present today; floor is the 4 the spec names.
